title: Hof operation journal (v2, backup/restore only)
description: /var/lib/hof/state/journal/<operationId>.json for a backup or restore operation - the durable, per-operation-run header record on the target. Scoped strictly to operationKind backup/restore, never apply: the existing apply executor (scripts/operation-journal.mjs, unchanged by this item) reads and writes operation-journal-v1 exclusively and always will, for every apply run, old or new - there is no migration of apply onto v2 in this item. Written once at operation start (immutable except `status`/`committedGeneration`, updated only by the same operationId that created it); individual attempts are recorded separately as an append-only operation-event-v2 log this journal's own operationId ties them to (a genuinely different resumability contract from apply's own operation-event-v1 - see operation-event-v2.schema.json's own description for why). A pre-existing journal written before this ADR has no operationKind field and does not validate against this schema - an executor must still read and safely resume it as operation-journal-v1 (implicit "apply"), never refuse it outright just because the field is absent; that case is unaffected by this schema being backup/restore-only, since a pre-ADR journal was always an apply journal anyway. Never holds a secret value, decrypted content, an environment dump, or an SSH private-key path - safe to read, copy, or attach to a bug report without a second sanitization pass.

operationKind.description: Which of the two new operation state machines produced this journal - never apply (see this schema's own top-level description). Decides which plan schema `plan` below was validated against before being embedded (backup-plan-v1 for backup, restore-plan-v1 for restore - enforced below, not merely documented) and this journal's own committedGeneration semantics (see below).

approvedPlanId.description: The exact plan this run was approved against (--approve-plan-id) - equal to plan.planId below by construction, regardless of operationKind. Schema cannot compare the two fields directly (no $data references are used in this repo); scripts/backup-ids.mjs's own bundle validators and this item's contract tests enforce the equality that would otherwise only ever be prose.

plan.description: The full, exact plan document this operation was approved against - not just its planId. Loosely typed here on purpose (no schema in this repo cross-references another by $id) - already validated against the schema matching operationKind before ever being embedded. Its own apiVersion is still constrained below (backup-plan-v1 for backup, restore-plan-v1 for restore) - the one piece of the embedded document's own shape this schema can and does check directly, even without a full cross-schema $ref.

inputDigests.description: Every input this specific run is bound to, fixed at journal creation and never recomputed from a live file again mid-run - independent of, and a defense-in-depth check against, the same values plan above already embeds. Shape depends on operationKind (enforced below): backup binds the signed release, the signed backup-tool-lock, and the exact applied backup-policy-v1 this plan was built against; restore binds the HISTORICAL signed release the backup was originally taken under, the signed backup-tool-lock, the backup-manifest-v1 embedded in the pinned snapshot, and the recovery kit.

status.description: in-progress: the operation is running, or was interrupted before its own evidence.write step ever ran - the only state in which --resume of this SAME operationId is valid, since evidence is not yet durably recorded. succeeded: the finally block and evidence.write both completed, and for backup every configured destination's own snapshot succeeded (a partial result is a failure here, recorded separately, honestly, in backup-evidence-v1's own status field). failed: evidence.write already ran (so evidence for whatever this operationId actually achieved - including a real partial backup result - is already durably, immutably recorded), and this specific journal is terminal: a retried attempt is always a genuinely NEW operationId (and so a fresh backupSequence/backupId for backup), never a --resume of this one. "failed" is therefore never a mid-operation, still-resumable state - that state is always in-progress.

committedGeneration.description: backup: always null, even on success - a backup never mutates current.json or the generation at all. restore: the restored SOURCE generation once state.restore succeeds, carried forward verbatim, never incremented - this is the same installation's history continuing on new hardware, not a new applied change. Null for the entire lifetime of a run that never reaches its own commit point, including every failed one, regardless of kind.

allOf.description: The status/committedGeneration/operationKind pairing this schema's own field descriptions above already document, actually enforced - reusing operation-journal-v1's own already-reviewed if/then/else mechanism (2026-08-31).
plan.apiVersion must actually match operationKind - a backup journal can never embed a restore-plan-v1 document or vice versa.
inputDigests is a closed, kind-specific shape - never the other kind's fields, never both at once.

ADR 0006 review: operation-journal-v1's own targetBinding left this pairing unenforced by schema (prose-only) - v2 (this schema) closes it. Not backported to operation-journal-v1 itself, which stays untouched.
